title: Surprises vs. expectations
summary: The [[surprise]] is actual minus [[consensus-forecast]], but the reaction also depends on what was already [[priced-in|priced in]] and how traders were positioned. The same number can bring different reactions on different days.
unreliableWhen: When positioning is unclear, when the consensus is not what traders really expected, when other parts of a report matter more than the headline, or when a bigger story dominates.
goodExample: A learner compares the calm and crowded fictional Westmark inflation scenarios: same +0.4 surprise, different run-ups. They write a different most-plausible reaction for each and one outcome that would prove them wrong.
badExample: A learner decides 'better than expected means up' and ignores a three-week run-up in which many traders had already bought. The price falls on the news.
